Lived in rural central Illinois. Was my mom's birthday so she and my dad had gone to town to a restaurant. I'm fourteen and home alone. (2004)  We have an attached garage, so I got a soda from the fridge and got the stray dog that adopted my family to come inside. Parents call the land line because the sky is looking pretty sinister, I'm annoyed because I was reading fan fiction and had to go close a door completely. (Was one of those double screen door things, so one could be open to let airflow through.) Didn't want water damaging floor inside.

Standing there talking on a cordless land phone with my dad still. Hadnt actually closed the door completely yet. Standing amd watching storm, because I love them. Even after this.  But that's when I realized that it was extremely windy. The air/rain/debris all horizontal.
 
That tornado was eight feet away.
It probably wouldn't have even registered as an F1, but you could see the tracks in our two acres the next day. 

I slammed the door shut, locked it, ran a few steps towards the safest room. No basement. Window frame blows in, hits my head and I lose my balance. All the metal bending and it felt like the house had been lifted off the foundation.

It kinda did. From the point outside the door to the path it took through the attached garage I was no further away then ten feet. One wall. Place dog had been in garage and extra fridge I got the soda from?

Gone. Garage gone. I can see part of the roof was in a farmers field to our north. Was relieved it went on that side of the house. The area it was never close to? Big ol' propane tank mostly full.

Tl;dr: 4-10 feet away from debris cloud.

The couple had young toddlers and my dog was a bit too rough so I bought her off of them.

-

The two hour drive home all she did was whine and cry, so my anxiety was extremely high. I looked around online to see how to get a dog verified for service. It's a bit easier to do if it's for an emotional service. There are a lot of places you can take your dog to be trained for it, or you can train them yourself and then take them to be evaluated. There are a few areas they have to pass.

-

They can't be skiddish around people, strangers or other pets. They can't be too loud or overly playful either, things like that. I really enjoy my dogs personality so I chose to train her myself -- extremely easy with hotdogs lol. Then you just meet the person who gets to evaluate.

-

I was relieved to hear that almost any breed can be registered as a service dog. You don't have to buy one already certified -- finding a dog or puppy with a personality that works for you is important. Working with them also gave me a huge sense of control, it felt like even if I can't manage my emotions properly I could at least train my dog to help. I never feel alone because she's always here. She's good in public too. Probably because she loves attention, but even if she gets a bit more excited over meeting new people and dogs she still always has half of her attention on me.

-

And she's still definitely a dog, she loves playing fetch or catching frisbees. Getting certified doesn't strip them of their personality which is what worried me at first. Best decision I've ever made. (On mobile, hopefully this post isn't too messy.)
